subject: Boston Avenue Zoning Veto Override
overview: The City Council overrode Mayor Lungo-Koehn's veto of the Boston Avenue corridor rezoning to permit purpose-built student housing by right in the BA3 subdistrict. The council also questioned the administration over fire department labor grievances, reallocated school capital funds, and advanced discussions on a Tufts University PILOT framework.

items.title: Routine Business and Recognitions
items.summary: Approved several community event resolutions, accepted the September 29 meeting minutes, and adopted a Committee of the Whole report on the zoning RFP.

items.title: Fire Department Labor Grievances and Legal Funding
items.summary: Referred a slate of questions to the administration regarding outside legal spending, withheld firefighter educational credits, and the status of an external audit of city legal practices.

items.title: School Capital Stabilization Reallocations
items.summary: Approved reallocating Medford Public Schools capital stabilization funds toward elementary school intercom replacements and various facility repairs.

items.title: Tufts PILOT and Community Benefits Framework
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Committee of the Whole to examine creating a PILOT commission and negotiating formal community benefits agreements with Tufts University.

items.title: Boston Avenue Rezoning Mayoral Veto Override
items.summary: Voted to override Mayor Lungo-Koehn's veto of the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District zoning amendment after defeating a motion to require a special permit for purpose-built student housing in the BA3 subdistrict. The council also requested that the administration remove disputed statements concerning the council's prior vote from the city website.

items.title: Tabled Business
items.summary: Tabled items addressing city charter implementation, a civil service exemption, police chief search consultant funding, and a supplemental appropriation for the law department to the next regular meeting.

items.title: Public Participation: Rebuttal by Micah Kesselman
items.summary: Heard a public statement from resident Micah Kesselman disputing statements made by the mayor in the Tufts Daily and criticizing the use of police inquiries into political organizers.
